chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Qatadah, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Umayyah ibn 'Ali al-Qaysi, from one of those who narrated it, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

He said to me: “The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله passes over the Sirat, followed by 'Ali, and al-Hasan follows 'Ali, and al-Husayn follows al-Hasan. When they reach its middle, al-Mukhtar calls out to al-Husayn عليه السلام: ‘O Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, I sought vengeance for your blood.’ Then the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله says to al-Husayn عليه السلام, ‘Answer him.’ So al-Husayn عليه السلام plunges into the Fire as though he were a swooping, crushing eagle, and he brings al-Mukhtar out, blackened like charcoal. And if his heart were split open, their love would be found in his heart.”

key_terms.أَجِبْهُ: answer him; a command addressed to al-Husayn عليه السلام
key_terms.الصِّرَاطَ: the bridge or path traversed in the hereafter
key_terms.النَّارِ: the Fire, referring to punishment in the hereafter
key_terms.الْمُخْتَارُ: al-Mukhtar, the figure mentioned as calling upon al-Husayn عليه السلام
key_terms.حُبُّهُمَا: love for the two of them, referring contextually to devotion within his heart

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about al-Mukhtar, the Sirat, and the intercession of al-Husayn عليه السلام in the afterlife?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a scene of the afterlife involving the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام at the Sirat, and the calling of al-Mukhtar to al-Husayn عليه السلام. It portrays al-Mukhtar as one who sought vengeance for al-Husayn عليه السلام, while also indicating a complex final state expressed through his being taken out of the Fire and the presence of love for them in his heart.
